cards.label: Bermondsey — James's unit
cards.text: Archie has taken the end of James's bench, his phone propped against a jar of powder. James is pretending not to watch.

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Up to now you've run every order yourself. Fetch it, carry it, hand it over. That's a job, not a business."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "The pearl order comes every week. Say yes once and it keeps coming. That's a recurring order, and you've been running it by hand."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Now the clever bit. Tap 'Delegate to Sales' and it's mine. I watch the stock, I hand it over when it's there, I chase the money. You don't touch it."

cards.speaker: James
cards.text: "The pearls will be mine. Owen's ore goes in, my pearls come out. The arrangement works without you in the room, which is the only test of an arrangement."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "So here's the test. Two of these, each running a full week with no help from you. Start whenever. A short first week counts if nobody touches it."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Help means handing the goods over yourself, making the thing it asks for, tending any of Owen's veins, moving what it wants out of your stash, or buying the calc it wants. Do any of that and that week doesn't count."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "Everything else is yours. Other veins, other crafting, the Collective, whoever you're fighting this week. And if I buy calc for an order out of the pot, that's the business doing its job. Doesn't count against you."

cards.speaker: Archie
cards.text: "If you've not taken a weekly ore order yet, six time or six life is still on BizBrief. Pick whichever you can keep up with."
James goes back to his bench. Archie puts his phone face down beside the hourglass and leaves it there.
